rules.sentence: Objectives: Differentiate oral lichen planus from similar lichenoid and autoimmune conditions using targeted history-taking, thorough clinical assessment, and histopathologic analysis.
Implement evidence-based, individualized strategies for managing oral lichen planus while minimizing adverse events.
The oral variant, oral lichen planus (OLP), is a chronic condition characterized by periods of relapse and remission, requiring long-term symptomatic treatment and surveillance (see Image.
Approximately 15% of patients with OLP develop cutaneous lesions, and around 20% develop genital lesions.
Lichen planus comprises a chronic inflammatory disease affecting the skin, hair follicles, nails, and mucosal surfaces, with predominant involvement of the skin and oral mucosa.

Cutaneous involvement is typically self-limiting and presents as violaceous, pruritic papules with overlying reticular white striae (Wickham striae), most commonly affecting the trunk or extremities, including the wrists and ankles.
Genital manifestations in women may include erythema, erosions, white reticulated plaques, labial resorption, or scarring.
In men, lesions may appear as annular, papulosquamous plaques on the glans penis, occasionally associated with dysuria and dyspareunia.
